text:
leo: Anyone else hit weird overload inference when bundling the sdk for edge? Local node dev: fine. esbuild -> edge: TS inference collapses and CI throws silly errors.

emily: I've seen this with generic overloads where the public API returns a conditional type that references an external type. Bundlers + ESM type emit can fail to name the dependency -> TS2742-ish. What exact error are you seeing?

leo: Build log from CI: 

dev-ci-bot: ```
> yarn workspace sample build
> esbuild src/edge.ts --bundle --format=esm --target=es2020 --outfile=dist/edge.js
TS ERROR: node_modules/@redwood/sdk/index.d.ts:8:19 - error TS2742: Exported variable 'createClient' has or is using name 'Opaque<'unknown'>' from external module "@types/external" but cannot be named.
error Command failed with exit code 2.
```

pranav: Opaque<unknown> -> yeah that's a classic. TS can't emit a name for a type that sits behind conditional or inferred 'unknown'. Two quick directions: 1) make the SDK typedefs avoid anonymous conditional types in exported signatures (we did this in a later patch) or 2) alter the consumer tsconfig so the emitter can resolve names.

leo: Is there a minimal tsconfig we can slap in the sample so newcomers don't hit this? Right now the sample uses a pretty permissive default.

emily: Minimal that helped me for edge samples: 

```json
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "target": "ES2020",
    "module": "ESNext",
    "moduleResolution": "NodeNext",
    "preserveValueImports": true,
    "importsNotUsedAsValues": "preserve",
    "skipLibCheck": true,
    "esModuleInterop": true
  }
}
```

pranav: Also try adding a types shim in the sample as a fallback. If the SDK exports something like: 

```ts
// in @redwood/sdk
export function createClient<T = unknown>(opts: Options<T>): Client<T>;
```

then the shim can import the problematic external type and re-export a named alias so dts knows the name: 

```ts
// types/alias.d.ts
import type { ExternalOpaque } from '@types/external';
export type ExternalOpaqueNamed = ExternalOpaque;
```

leo: That worked locally for me, thanks. But feels hacky. Should we change SDK?

pranav: Yes, SDK change would be to avoid leaking anonymous conditional types at the top-level. Two concrete fixes are: - introduce a small internal named type for the conditional and export the named type instead of inlining it into the function signature, or - add a typesVersions/package export mapping so TS picks a simpler types file for edge/bundled consumers.

docs: If you're adding a shim or tsconfig, please open a PR to add an "edge-quickstart-tsconfig" and a one-liner to the onboarding that calls out TS2742 troubleshooting. I'll curate it into the quickstart guide.

emily: One more note: sometimes the difference between unknown vs any matters for inference. If you see callers getting weird any, try switching generic defaults to unknown + explicit constraints. That avoids accidental widening during inference.

leo: Good call. I'll file an issue on the SDK to propose the named-type fix and meanwhile add the tsconfig + shim to the sample. I'll ping when PRs are up. Thanks! :raised_hands:
